head: 6b91dea8b89f7c0480a0373ebd7d94d03a575de0
summary:
I ran the tooling as it stands at 6b91dea, live on this machine: the published app, its real WPF window on the real GPU and desktop compositor, and T-005's tree on real D:\ (D:\fsa-sl080-temp).

**Height (the slice's main question): the builder's verdict reproduced.** My own batch (artifacts/sl080/validate-height, 17 runs, exit 0) read no-measurable-difference: 860 px higher in 5 of 8 pairs, median ratio 1.021, sd 0.343, smallest detectable ratio 1.48, no order effect. The builder's height-4 read 4 of 8, median 1.026, detectable 1.35.
- All 17 of my runs, plus 3 refusal-check runs, sized the window at "when":"Initialized", actual height equal to asked.
- The scan's first move waited about 334–355 ms in both arms. That confirms the arms are equal at load (O-030). The three build attempts spent on where the hook sets the height are closed by measurement.
- Rereading the builder's height-4 runs.jsonl from a temp copy gave its figures exactly: 4 of 8, median 1.026, detectable 1.35.

**Trace: the attribution reproduced under the current sizing.** trace-2 had been run under the superseded sizing. My batch (validate-trace, exit 0) read render-path, next -Plan Render.
- Traced runs stalled 4 of 4 and untraced 4 of 4, so tracing did not mask the stall.
- Three traced runs read RENDER-PATH and one SPLIT, sampled every 1 ms per the traces themselves.
- The scan's first move waited 337.4 ms, 129.8 ms after StartScan, with 93.6% of the stretch in DUCE+Channel.SyncFlush.
- The SPLIT run's rescan stretch had 48.7% under DependencyObject.SetValue. That matches the doc's account of the longer rescan stalls.

**Height refusal, live.** -LowHeight 620 stopped at run 2 with "height not applied (620/644)", exit 1.

**Render: did NOT reproduce what the doc reports from render-2.** render-2 was run under the superseded sizing and read render-thread-or-dwm-not-gpu (median 1.048). My batch (validate-render) read inconclusive:
- median software/hardware ratio 0.56 (sd 0.368, detectable 2.15);
- software lower in 3 of 4 pairs;
- the scan phase in software at 61–79 ms against 335–347 ms in hardware, 4 of 4.

This leans towards the GPU/present side, like the superseded render-1. The doc's conclusion still holds: whether the flush waits on the GPU is not settled. But its render-2 table and reading are now contradicted in direction by a batch run under the current tool. This does not break any acceptance criterion, which is why the verdict is passes.

**Batch-to-batch drift.** The ~1.3 s stall kind hit 1 of 16 counted runs in my Height batch, against 7 of 16 in height-4. primaryMs came from the rescan in 14 of 16 of my runs, against the scan in 14 of 16 there. Both batches still read the same.

**Other checks.** Self-tests passed: T005Batch 33/33, StallStacks 13/13. Fitness: all 62 rules hold. src/ has zero diff from the base, 97dc576.

**How the 12 criteria were checked.** Five were confirmed live (4, 6, 9, 10, 11); 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and 8 only through canned fixtures running the real code, because their conditions never came up live; 12 rests on the spikes the doc cites.

checks.evidence: Empty output. The 60 changed files are under tests/window, docs/design, .taad.

PASSED: 33 fixtures, exit 0. Includes height-drift, height-quiet, stop-height-refused/silent, stop-no-line, stop-crashed, summary-phase-never-reached, trace-masks, trace-masks-10ms, trace-split, trace-render, trace-cannot-read, and arm-variables (12 taken out, 8 left).
PASSED: 13 fixtures, exit 0. unresolved and external-frames give CANNOT-READ, render-chain and render-mixed give RENDER-PATH, pump-only gives SPLIT.
62 rules checked against 116 parsed files. Every declared rule holds, including the widened 'the shipped app carries no test seam' (FSA_HOOK_, FSA_T005_, tests[\\/]window over src/**).

checks.what: Live Height batch, 860 vs 644 px, on real D:\ (independent replication of the delivered verdict)
checks.evidence: Exit 0 (07:29–07:39). VERDICT no-measurable-difference. 16 of 16 runs stalled; 860 px higher in 5 of 8 pairs; median ratio 1.021; logRatioSd 0.343; detectableRatio 1.48; orderEffect false (first run of its pair higher in 5 of 8). Pair ratios: 0.871, 0.899, 1.015, 0.551, 1.027, 1.893, 1.178, 1.032. Every run: exitReason closed, BelowNormal, .NET 10.0.12, render Default; tree root D:\fsa-sl080-temp\fsa-window-cases\...\tree.

checks.what: The hook sizes every arm before the window has a handle (O-030 fix), and the arms are equal at load
checks.evidence: 17 of 17 sized lines read "when":"Initialized", with actual equal to asked (860 or 644), ms 215–561. Scan-phase longest wait at the first move was 334.3–352.0 ms at 860 px and 337.4–355.1 ms at 644 px. Exceptions: 860 px 464.2, 872.3 and 1,382.5 ms (the last two on later moves); 644 px 438.8 and 730.1 ms.

checks.what: The builder's height-4 verdict recomputes from its stored runs
checks.command: copy artifacts\sl080\height-4\runs.jsonl to %TEMP%\sl080-validate-reread; T005Batch.ps1 -Plan Height -Reread -Out <that copy>
checks.evidence: Exit 0. no-measurable-difference, '860 px higher in 4 of 8 pairs', medianRatio 1.026, detectableRatio 1.35, orderEffect False. Identical to the doc. Temp copy deleted afterwards.

checks.what: Live Trace batch under the current (Initialized) sizing. trace-2 was run under the superseded sizing.
checks.evidence: Exit 0. VERDICT render-path, next -Plan Render. Traced stalls 4 of 4 (median 605.6 ms), untraced 4 of 4 (median 618.1 ms), so no masking. sampleMs 1 taken from the traces. Runs 1, 4 and 8 read RENDER-PATH (97%, 72%, 91% of the stretch in the synchronous render). Run 5 read SPLIT on its rescan: 48.7% under DependencyObject.SetValue, only the pump common. Run 5's scan stretch: wait 337.4 ms, 129.8 ms after StartScan, 93.6% leaf in DUCE+Channel.SyncFlush, under HwndTargetFilterMessage (63%) and MediaContextNotificationWindow.MessageFilter (30.6%), unreadable 1%. UI-thread idle 47–53%.

checks.what: Live refusal of a height the window cannot take (MinHeight 644)
checks.evidence: Warm-up and run 1 ran at 860 px. Run 2 logged sized asked 620, actual 644, when Initialized, then error 'height not applied (620/644)'. The batch printed 'STOPPED at run 2' and exited 1 (the intended stop), before run 3.

checks.what: Live Render batch under the current sizing (does render-2's reading reproduce?)
checks.evidence: Exit 0 and the tool behaved correctly, but the delivered finding did not reproduce. VERDICT inconclusive: medianRatio 0.56, logRatioSd 0.368, detectableRatio 2.15, hardware stalls 4 of 4. Pair software/hardware primary: 308.4/699.0, 288.3/527.9, 419.8/402.9, 225.9/393.6, so software lower in 3 of 4. Scan phase in software 61.3–79.1 ms against 334.9–347.4 ms in hardware, 4 of 4. The doc's render-2 (superseded sizing) read render-thread-or-dwm-not-gpu at median 1.048; this batch points the other way, towards the GPU/present side, but by the rule it is inconclusive. The doc's overall 'whether the flush waits on the GPU is not settled' still stands.

checks.what: Temp case folders cleaned up per run on D:\
checks.evidence: 1 folder after 43 live runs. Runs do not accumulate trees on D:\. D:\fsa-sl080-temp itself is the builder's and was left in place.

Not run separately: src/ is unchanged from 97dc576, and build-check recorded a clean build there (0 warnings, 0 errors). The live batches rebuilt and loaded the hook and ran the published exe without error.

checks.what: Scan of D:\'s actual contents rather than T-005's synthetic tree on D:\
checks.evidence: Whether the brief means this is an open design-slice question for a person. Not answered, so not run.

checks.what: Traced reading of the ~1.3 s stall kind
checks.evidence: None of my 4 traced runs hit it. In my Height batch it appeared only in the warm-up (1,380.2 ms) and run 12 (1,382.5 ms), both untraced.

criteria.criterion: 1. Attribute a UI-thread stall — when unelevated EventPipe sampling produces mostly unresolved/external frames on this UI thread
criteria.how: By code only: StallStacks fixtures 'unresolved' (70%) and 'external-frames' (80%) give CANNOT-READ, and T005Batch fixtures trace-cannot-read and trace-reader-crash route to cannot-read, next FSA_HOOK_MSGLOG. Live, this condition never came up: my traces had at most 1% unreadable. The fallback itself is contract only, as the design allowed.

criteria.criterion: 2. Attribute a UI-thread stall — when the act of tracing changes the timing enough that traced runs stop stalling
criteria.how: By code only: fixtures trace-masks (next: -SampleMs 10) and trace-masks-10ms (next: in-process fallback) pass, and the rate is taken from the traces' samplingNs. Live: traced 4 of 4 against untraced 4 of 4 in my Trace batch, so masking did not occur and the branch did not fire.

criteria.criterion: 3. Attribute a UI-thread stall — when different traced runs land on different blocking methods
criteria.how: By fixture: trace-split gives SPLIT. Live: my Trace batch had 3 RENDER-PATH and 1 SPLIT, which the 3-or-more rule correctly read as render-path, not NAMED.

criteria.criterion: 4. Measure 860 vs 620 px — when the stall drifts over minutes independent of height
criteria.how: Live ABBA batch on D:\: orderEffect false (5 of 8), no-measurable-difference, alongside large between-batch drift (the ~1.3 s kind in 1 of 16 runs here against 7 of 16 in height-4). Fixture height-drift passes. The orderEffect flag is still symmetric (≤1 or ≥7 of 8) against the design's ≥7/8, a recorded code-review drift item.

criteria.criterion: 5. Measure 860 vs 620 px — when the batch happens to run quiet
criteria.how: By code only: fixture height-quiet gives no-stall-this-batch, next 'run again'. Live, all 16 runs stalled, so the branch was not exercised.

criteria.criterion: 6. Measure 860 vs 620 px — when the hook cannot apply the requested height (MinHeight clamp)
criteria.how: Live: -LowHeight 620 on D:\ sized at Initialized to actual 644, the hook refused 'height not applied (620/644)', and the batch stopped at run 2 with exit 1. Fixtures stop-height-refused and stop-height-silent pass. The low arm is 644, since 620 cannot be had at HEAD.

criteria.criterion: 7. Summarize a T-005 run — when a phase is never reached
criteria.how: By code only: fixture summary-phase-never-reached feeds a hook log through WindowCases.ps1's real ConvertTo-T005Summary and stops the batch on the null rescan phase. Every live run reached both phases.

criteria.criterion: 8. Run the batch driver — when a run crashes or writes no summary line
criteria.how: By code only: fixtures stop-no-line (run 5 wrote no summary line) and stop-crashed (no-close, exit -1073740791) stop with exit 1. No live run crashed; the refusal run shows the same stop path live for a hook error.

criteria.criterion: 9. Name the blocking frame — when the stretch lands inside WPF's synchronous render path
criteria.how: Live: 3 of 4 traced runs read RENDER-PATH, not NAMED, even where blockedUnder was DUCE+Channel.SyncFlush (run 1, 97%). The batch routed to -Plan Render. The follow-up Render batch was inconclusive (median 0.56, detectable 2.15), contradicting render-2's direction; see summary.

criteria.criterion: 10. Compare de51999 against HEAD — when de51999 predates FolderTree
criteria.how: Spike de51999-runs-under-current-t005 (no-go, 'the window has no FolderTree'). The doc records it and substitutes a same-build height ABBA on HEAD, which I ran live and which reproduced.

criteria.criterion: 11. Compare de51999 against HEAD — when 33 files / +3185 lines differ beyond height
criteria.how: Spike only-width-differs-de51999-to-head (no-go) is quoted in the doc's 'What was measured instead' section. The height is the only difference between arms, verified live: every run sized at Initialized with actual equal to its arm's height.

criteria.criterion: 12. Rule out non-UI causes — GC pause growth; outside CPU load or worker count
criteria.how: By citation of settled spikes, not re-run: rescan-stall-is-gc-suspension (conditional, ≤1%, holds for heaps up to ~110 MB, which T-005's tree is within) and stall-rides-competing-cpu-load (go, 18/18). The doc cites both but does not carry the GC spike's heap-size condition.

obligations.evidence: My live Height batch: 17 of 17 sized lines 'when':'Initialized', actual equal to asked. The scan's first-move wait was 334–352 ms at 860 px and 337–355 ms at 644 px, so the arms are equal at load.
Live -LowHeight 620: sized actual 644, hook error 'height not applied (620/644)', batch STOPPED at run 2, exit 1.
My verdict.json carries logRatioSd 0.343 and detectableRatio 1.48 beside no-measurable-difference.
My live Trace verdict.json: sampleMs 1, sampleMsFrom 'the traces'. Each stacks-n.json has samplingNs 1000000.
Live traced runs with blockedUnder DUCE+Channel.SyncFlush read RENDER-PATH, not NAMED, and the batch routed to -Plan Render.

not_reached: The delivered Render reading is not stable. My live Render batch under the current sizing read inconclusive (median software/hardware 0.56). Software took the scan's first-move stall from ~340 ms to 61–79 ms in 4 of 4 pairs, while render-2, run under the superseded sizing, read render-thread-or-dwm-not-gpu (median 1.048). The doc's render-2 table no longer describes the tool as it stands. The recorded 8-pair Render batch would need a schedule change (Render is 2 blocks = 4 pairs) and was not done.
A scan of what is really on D:\ (the design-slice open question): every batch here used T-005's synthetic 100,000-file tree on D:\, not D:\'s own contents.
The GC-share result is conditional on heaps up to ~110 MB. A real multi-GB scan's rescan stall was not checked for GC share.

What the render thread, the desktop compositor (DWM) and the GPU do during SyncFlush: EventPipe does not see them. An elevated ETW/WPR capture is an open question for a person, and neither named elevation operation (whoami, read-denied-folders) would reach it, so none was requested.
A person dragging the window (DefWindowProc's modal size/move loop). Every stack came from the hook's programmatic SetWindowPos.
A traced reading of the ~1.3 s stall kind (the brief's 1,318.5 ms): none of my traced runs hit it.
The CANNOT-READ and tracing-masks branches, and the FSA_HOOK_MSGLOG fallback (contract only), never occurred live.
Normal process priority: the sandbox pins every child process at BelowNormal, so every run here was BelowNormal, unlike a person's own launch.
Other GPUs, DPI settings or machines: all runs were on this PC's work area of 1032 px, render tier 2.
